evals.prompt: We just decided to switch our primary database from PostgreSQL to Supabase because of its built-in row-level security and real-time subscriptions — it fits our multi-tenant SaaS model much better. Firebase and PlanetScale were considered but didn't make the cut. Please save this decision.
evals.expected_output: A well-structured decision file created at memory/decisions/<slug>/README.md with MAGI-compatible YAML frontmatter (doc-id, title, description, category: decision, created, last-updated, tags), a body covering the decision statement, reasoning, alternatives considered (Firebase, PlanetScale), trade-offs, and affected areas. MEMORY.md updated with a pointer under Recent Decisions. Confirmation message to the user.
expectations: A decision file is created at a path under memory/decisions/ with a README.md as the entry point
The decision file includes MAGI-compatible YAML frontmatter with fields: doc-id, title, description, category set to 'decision', created, last-updated, and tags
The decision file body includes all four required sections: the decision itself, reasoning for choosing Supabase, alternatives considered (naming both Firebase and PlanetScale), and trade-offs
MEMORY.md is updated to include a new pointer to the decision under a Recent Decisions section
The agent confirms to the user what was saved and where, in a clear summary message

evals.prompt: I've noticed you keep formatting your summaries as prose paragraphs but I actually prefer bullet points — clear, short, scannable. Please remember this preference for all future responses.
evals.expected_output: A preference file created at memory/preferences/<slug>.md with MAGI-compatible YAML frontmatter. Body clearly states the preference (bullet points over prose), the context (all response summaries), and the date it was stated. MEMORY.md updated with a one-line preference entry under User Preferences. Confirmation to user.
expectations: A preference file is created at a path under memory/preferences/ with a .md extension
The preference file includes MAGI-compatible YAML frontmatter with category set to 'preference'
The preference file body clearly articulates the preference for bullet points over prose paragraphs

MEMORY.md is updated with a new entry under a User Preferences section referencing this formatting preference, OR if MEMORY.md is already at or above 4 KB, preferences/README.md is updated instead — either outcome is acceptable
The agent confirms to the user what was saved and where, including whether MEMORY.md was updated
